description: Expose MentorAgent as a universal AI backend from any ASP.NET Core application. Adds a SignalR hub (/mentor-hub), SSE streaming endpoint (/mentor/chat), MCP server, and A2A agent — no Blazor required.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.1

		The first release candidate. No new features. The transport had no automated coverage at all before this cycle; it now has 60 in-process tests plus a cross-transport parity pass that compares the SignalR hub and the SSE stream against the same 30 checks. That comparison is what found the three defects below, and none of them was reachable by any in-process test.

		=== The SSE stream - behaviour changes, act on these ========================
		- BREAKING - {"type":"completed"} now means THE TURN IS OVER. It previously fired when the streaming segment ended, which is not the same thing: a turn parked on a human confirmation ended "completed" while the action had been withheld, so the client was told the turn had succeeded and was given no action id to approve. The assistant had already said "I'll go ahead and do that", and nothing ran. A client that treated "completed" as "the answer is finished" keeps working; a client that used it to decide the request had SUCCEEDED must now also watch for confirmationRequired.
		- NEW FRAME - {"type":"confirmationRequired","actionId":"...","tool":"...","message":"..."}. Answer it with POST /mentor/approve?actionId=...&approved=true|false on a second request while the stream is open, and the parked turn resumes. Verified end to end against a live model.
		- NEW FRAME - {"type":"navigation","url":"..."}. navigate_to previously emitted nothing over SSE while the model announced the move, and the server README promised this event on this transport.
		- FIXED - {"type":"cards"} was documented, subscribed, assembled - and lost. Four async void handlers wrote straight to one HttpResponse, which does not allow overlapping writes, inside an empty catch block. A frame lost in silence is indistinguishable from a frame that was never raised. All frames now go through a single ordered writer, and a write that fails is logged instead of swallowed.
		- The stream's complete frame set is now documented as a table in the README: chunk, cards, navigation, confirmationRequired, completed, error.

		=== Security ================================================================
		- SECURITY - the MCP endpoint published every [MentorAction] with no gate, including actions restricted by RequiredRoles and actions marked RequiresConfirmation. Separate process, no principal, permissive CORS by default. Gated actions are now withheld and the withheld set is logged with its reason.
		- SECURITY - the same hole existed a second time for actions gated by the options.RequiresApproval predicate rather than by the attribute. Both routes now fail closed. This is a behaviour change with no opt-out; see the core package's notes for why.

		=== A2A ====================================================================
		- FIXED - four of AgentCardInfo's five properties (IconUrl, Provider, DocumentationUrl and the version override) never reached the published agent card. The card's only audience is another machine, so the symptom was a remote agent receiving less metadata than promised - at best a missing icon in somebody else's directory.
		- CORRECTED - Tags was documented as "included in the Agent Card for discovery purposes". It cannot be: the A2A specification attaches tags to individual skills, not to the card. It is now documented as reserved and not published. A false row in a table is worse than a missing one, because it gets believed.
		- The endpoint gate now throws at startup naming both the option and where to set it, rather than mapping nothing and leaving a peer taking 404s against an endpoint the operator believes is live.
		- Trap worth knowing: with A2AServerUrl unset the card advertises a bare path. Still valid, still served, and useless to any client that does not share your host.

		=== Documentation corrections (each of these silently broke a custom client) ==
		- The streaming event is StreamingChunk, not ReceiveChunk.
		- Navigation arrives as NavigationRequested, not NavigateTo.
		- The protocol reference was missing Cards and HostedToolsDeclared; all 18 server-to-client events are now listed, together with the two client-to-server methods documented as do-not-use (CancelRequest, RespondToApproval - SignalR dispatches one hub call at a time per connection, so both deadlock; use the HTTP routes).
		- The endpoint table now lists /mentor/approve, /mentor/cancel, /mentor/admin/metrics and /mentor/tour.
		- Written down for the first time: a SignalR reconnect is a new connection id, therefore a new DI scope and a NEW CONVERSATION. That is deliberate - the per-connection scope is exactly what keeps two browsers apart - and the remedy is the session snapshot API. The README recommends withAutomaticReconnect() in six places and never said so.

		=== Known limitation ========================================================
		- The SSE stream forwards six of the hub's eighteen events - the six that decide what the user sees. GeneratedImages, RAG citations and the hosted-tool activity line are hub-only; a client on SSE will not receive them. This is a capability gap, not a promise broken: the events table is scoped to the hub by its column header. If you need them, use the hub.
